To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about x=1, we plug a=1 into the general formula to give

P3(x)=f(1)+f′(1)(x−1)+f″(1)2!(x−1)2+f‴(1)3!(x−1)3P3(x)=f(1)+f′(1)(x−1)+f″(1)2(x−1)2+f‴(1)6(x−1)3.

We need to compute f(1), f′(1), f″(1), and f‴(1), as follows:

f(x)=1x2⟹f(1)=112=1f′(x)=−2x3⟹f′(1)=−213=−2f″(x)=6x4⟹f″(1)=614=6f‴(x)=−24x5⟹f‴(1)=−2415=−24

Finally, we plug the results for f(1), f′(1), f″(1), and f‴(1) into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

P3(x)=(1)+(−2)⋅(x−1)+(6)2⋅(x−1)2+(−24)6⋅(x−1)3=1−2(x−1)+3(x−1)2−4(x−1)3.

Your Answer:
1, 3, 4
